related_questions.question: What is the survival rate for colon cancer?

text_blocks.snippet: The 5-year survival rate for colorectal cancer varies significantly based on the stage at diagnosis. For localized cancer, the rate is around 90%, while for distant (metastatic) cancer, it's around 14-15%. Overall, about 63% of people diagnosed with colorectal cancer are alive 5 years later, according to a study from 2013-2019.
snippet_highlighted_words: For localized cancer, the rate is around 90%, while for distant (metastatic) cancer, it's around 14-15%

list.title: Localized Cancer:
list.snippet: When the cancer is confined to the colon or rectum, the 5-year survival rate is very high, around 90%.

list.title: Regional Cancer:
list.snippet: If the cancer has spread to nearby tissues or lymph nodes, the 5-year survival rate is around 71%.

list.title: Distant Cancer:
list.snippet: When the cancer has spread to distant organs, the 5-year survival rate drops significantly to around 14-15%.

list.title: Overall:
list.snippet: The 5-year relative survival rate for all stages of colorectal cancer combined is about 63%.

text_blocks.snippet: Several factors influence survival rates, including:

list.title: Stage of cancer:
list.snippet: As mentioned above, the stage at diagnosis is the most significant factor.

list.title: Age:
list.snippet: Older individuals may have lower survival rates due to other health conditions.

list.title: Overall health:
list.snippet: Individuals with other serious health problems may have a harder time surviving colorectal cancer.

list.title: Treatment received:
list.snippet: Surgical removal of the tumor, chemotherapy, and radiation therapy can all improve survival rates.

text_blocks.snippet: Important Note: These are just general statistics, and individual outcomes can vary. Advances in treatment have led to improved survival rates over time, and ongoing research continues to seek further advancements.
